title: Relay gate role text stops repeating the Gate section's FAIL rule
lead: s424 added a `gate` role to `ai relay`'s Roles and `roles[]` (`src/slicer/ai.py`, the gate role text). Its sentence that the gate sends a FAIL back to the implementer restates the Gate section's rule, against s424's own aim of stating each rule once. Reword the role text to say what the gate is (read-only, decides) and point to Gate for what a FAIL does.
findings_note: s424 review 2026-10-30, later nit: the new `gate` Roles text "sends a FAIL back to the implementer" repeats the Gate section's "FAIL goes back to the implementer and then the gate again"
boundary: **Not in this slice:** any other contract wording, or a contract bump on its own (fold it into the next rule-changing contract bump, or ship it as text-only if nothing a role follows changes).

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: Each rule stated once keeps the contract from drifting when one copy is edited and the other is not.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `src/slicer/ai.py`: the `gate` entry in the Roles text and `roles[]`.
- `tests/test_ai.py`: extend `test_AiRelay_Text_StatesEachRuleOnce` with the FAIL-routing phrase.
- The contract golden fixture.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body: - `test_AiRelay_Text_StatesEachRuleOnce` counts the FAIL-goes-back rule once in `ai relay`.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Add the phrase to the once-only test; watch it go red.
2. Reword the gate role text; rebaseline the golden.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: - `python3 tests/affected.py --run`, then the full suite; `slicer check` passes.
